question: Last year, Frontex deployed 840 standing corps category 1 officers, 450 category 2 officers and 840 category 3 officers for joint operations in around 300 locations. They come from the Schengen Member States or the Frontex standing corps. 1.
How many of the 2 800 officers deployed in Frontex missions belong to the Frontex standing corps and what is their breakdown across the four categories?
Can the Commission list the countries where standing corps category 1 staff has been deployed and specify how many officers have been sent to each of these countries?
In which countries do these category 1 officers carry weapons provided by the host country and in which countries do they carry weapons issued by Frontex?
answer: 1. Overall, in mid-April 2024, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex) deployed approximately 870 Standing Corps Category C officers, 625 Category C officers, and 850 Category C officers in Member States, Schengen associated countries and third countries. These numbers are frequently subject to changes due to the evolving operational needs. 2.

Frontex is currently deploying the Standing Corps Category C officers in 19 Member States. These are Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia and Spain.

For the reason explained under the first question, the Commission cannot specify the number of Standing Corps Category C deployed in each of those Member States. 3. As sub-question 3 falls entirely under the responsibility of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency (Frontex), the Commission has asked the Agency to provide the details requested by the Honourable Member.
The Agency’s reply will be sent by the Commission to the Honourable Member as soon as possible.
